Charges, costs, and provenance

Source: vignettes/articles/costs.Rmd
costs.Rmd

Convert charges to costs

Charges are not costs. nis_cost() estimates hospital costs by multiplying charges by CCR_NIS, then expresses both cost and charges in a selected reference-year dollar using annual CPI-U indices.

charges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS) |>
  dplyr::collect()
adjusted <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2024)
head(adjusted[c("YEAR", "TOTCHG", "cost_adj", "charges_adj")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>    YEAR TOTCHG cost_adj charges_adj
#>   <int>  <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1  2020  14155    4975.      17156.
#> 2  2020  14190    4988.      17199.
#> 3  2020  14225    5000.      17241.
#> 4  2020  14260    5012.      17284.
#> 5  2020  14295    5025.      17326.
#> 6  2020  14330    5037.      17369.

cost_adj contains the estimated cost in 2024 dollars and charges_adj contains adjusted charges. These are synthetic amounts intended only to show the calculation.

Check provenance

The direct result records the source fields, price index, base year, multipliers, and invalid input counts.

nis_cost_provenance(adjusted)
#> $charge_field
#> [1] "TOTCHG"
#> 
#> $ccr_field
#> [1] "CCR_NIS"
#> 
#> $inflation_index
#> [1] "CPI-U All items, U.S. city average (annual average)"
#> 
#> $inflation_index_source
#> [1] "U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U All items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted, series CUUR0000SA0; annual averages"
#> 
#> $base_year
#> [1] 2024
#> 
#> $multipliers
#>   year multiplier
#> 1 2019   1.226992
#> 2 2020   1.212039
#> 
#> $rows_missing_or_invalid_ccr
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $rows_missing_charges
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $ccr_treatment
#> [1] "Missing, non-finite, zero, or negative CCR_NIS values produce NA cost_adj; charges_adj is retained."
#> 
#> $output_types
#>                  charges_adj                     cost_adj 
#> "Inflation-adjusted charges" "Estimated cost via CCR_NIS"

Missing or non-positive CCR values produce missing costs; the corresponding adjusted charge can still be present. Describe the CCR and inflation choices when reporting results.

nis_design(..., dollars = 2024) can add these adjusted values to the survey design when CCR_NIS and the selected charge column are kept.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Calling inflation-adjusted charges “costs” without applying a CCR.
  • Treating missing or invalid CCR values as zero cost.
  • Combining TOTCHG_2023 silently with earlier TOTCHG; its definition is different and the package documents the 2023 layout as unverified.
  • Dropping provenance attributes through later data-frame operations before recording the adjustment method.

See nis_cost(), nis_cost_provenance(), and nis_design().
